title: SimMIM: a Simple Framework for Masked Image Modeling
layout_note: An L-shaped path: the input photo cut into a 3x3 patch grid sits at the lower left, an arrow labelled 'Mask' runs right into a row of patches where masked ones are hatched squares, and the path then turns upward through an 'Encoder (e.g., ViT, Swin)' box and a 'One-layer Prediction Head' box to a row of blurry predicted patches compared with a row of original patches above via red double arrows labelled l1 loss.
grouping: No containers. The two model boxes are stacked, equal-width rectangles directly above the patch row; the prediction and target patch rows are stacked above them, aligned column by column with the masked positions below.
shapes_depth: Flat white rectangles with dark-red outlines and square corners for Encoder and Prediction Head. Patches are real photo thumbnails; masked patches are grey diagonal-hatched squares; predictions are the same crops shown blurred and faded. Arrows and loss double arrows are dark red.
proposed_highlight: A single accent colour (dark red) is used for all model boxes, arrows and loss marks, and the model boxes carry their names in plain text; the 'one-layer' head is named in its label to stress simplicity.
lesson: For masked prediction, stack the predicted patches directly under their target patches, column-aligned with the masked slots below, and join each pair with a short coloured double arrow labelled with the loss.
notes: Remembered venue: CVPR 2022 (not printed on the arXiv PDF's first page); year = arXiv preprint year.

arrangement.units: One unframed diagram: input grid at the lower left, a patch row along the bottom right, two stacked model boxes above it, and prediction/target patch rows at the top right.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo divided into a 3x3 grid of patches, then a row of patch thumbnails with masked ones drawn as hatched squares
arrangement.losses_at: top, as red vertical double arrows between each predicted patch and its original, with the 'l1 loss' label to the left of the row

taxonomy.task: masked image modelling pre-training by raw-pixel regression
taxonomy.note: paradigm: SimMIM is concurrent with MAE (both regress raw pixels of masked patches); listed under MAE as the closest founding masked-image-modelling method in the list

insights.structure: An L-shaped layout: a patch grid at lower left feeds a horizontal masked patch row, above which an encoder box and a one-layer head box are stacked, topped by predicted and target patch rows.
insights.data: Patches are real photo crops, masked ones are grey hatched squares, and predictions are the same crops rendered blurred and faded so prediction vs target reads by image quality.
insights.emphasis: One dark-red accent colours every model outline, arrow and loss double arrow, and only the masked columns have outputs above them, so the loss visibly applies to masked positions only.
insights.flow: Right along the bottom ('Mask' arrow), then up through encoder and head, and finally vertical red double arrows between the two top patch rows.
insights.avoid: The large empty region above the input grid at the upper left leaves the figure lopsided; the input could sit higher or the figure be tighter.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
